Bulk selection is in. Reload **http://maker:4001/app.html**.

**Block C — acting on several bookmarks at once.** Try this:

> 1. Each item now has a **checkbox** on its left. Tick **two or three** items. A dark **action bar** appears at the top showing how many are selected.
> 2. In that bar, type a tag (e.g. `review`) into the small box and press **Add tag** — it's added to all selected at once. **Remove tag** takes it back off them.
> 3. Try **Mark read later**, then **Archive** on the selection — watch the counts and views update together.
> 4. Use **"Select all N shown"** — this selects everything currently matching your search/view. To see it target a subset: first search `#reference`, then **Select all shown**, and apply an action only to those. Clear the search and note it acted on just that matched set.
> 5. Press **Delete…** in the bar — it asks once to confirm permanent deletion of the whole selection, mirroring the single-item safeguard.

A few things to check and decide:

- Is a **left-hand checkbox per row** the right way to pick items, with a **sticky action bar** at the top — or would you expect selection to work differently?
- **"Select all N shown"** deliberately means *everything matching the current search/view* (not every bookmark ever). Does scoping bulk actions to the current search/view match your intent?
- After an action, I **keep** the selection for tag/read changes but **clear** it after Archive/Unarchive/Delete (since those items leave the view). Does that feel right, or would you prefer it always clears, or always keeps?
